title: Calling Azure from ABAP Cloud Just Got Easier
author: DivyaBalakrishna
text:
The challenge every ABAP-on-Azure integration team faces 
 Developers who have called an Azure REST API from ABAP Cloud will find this familiar. Something simple, like archiving a document to Blob storage or querying the resource estate, means the same plumbing: hand built ` if_web_http_client ` requests, hand joined URLs, manual OAuth tokens, inline parsing, and retry, logging, and error handling rewritten each time. 
 In classic ABAP environments, teams relied on the established ABAP SDK for Azure . ABAP Cloud is different: a restricted, released API only model behind SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment and S/4HANA Cloud, where many classic patterns are gone, so teams fall back to hand rolled HTTP. That is repetitive, error prone, and hard to unit test, which is the gap this SDK closes. 
 Introducing the ABAP Cloud SDK for Azure 
 The ABAP Cloud SDK for Azure is a new open source client library for SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment and S/4HANA Cloud. In place of boilerplate, developers get a layered HTTP pipeline, Microsoft Entra ID credentials, typed exceptions, and typed service clients, so developers can write what they mean: 
 DATA(lo_blob) = NEW zcl_az_blob_client( 
 iv_account_name = 'mystorageacct' 
 io_credential = lo_credential ). 
 DATA(lo_blobs) = lo_blob->list_blobs( iv_container = 'my-container' ). 
 No manual HTTP, URL building, or token handling. The runtime handles it. 
 Built for ABAP Cloud 
 The project stays within ABAP Cloud's constraints: written entirely in ABAP for Cloud Development and using only released APIs, so it activates cleanly. 
 How it fits together 
 The SDK is layered. Each concern stays isolated, testable, and reused across every client. 
 HTTP pipeline: an ordered chain of policies for retry, authentication, logging, and transport. 
 Credentials: one interface for every credential type, with a token cache for valid tokens. 
 Typed exceptions: meaningful SDK errors, not raw status codes. 
 Typed models: responses map into ABAP structures, so developers work with fields, not strings. 
 Injection seam: every client accepts an optional transport, so tests swap in a double and run offline. 
 A service client stays thin, and the shape mirrors the official Azure SDKs, so it feels familiar. 
 Authentication: Entra ID first 
 Authentication is built around Microsoft Entra ID. Every credential implements the same interface: client secret (service principal), managed identity, an environment credential that reads configuration from a table, and a default credential that chains the available providers. 
 For Storage Blob access, prefer a User Delegation SAS, a short lived token signed by an Entra ID identity with no account key, then a direct Entra ID credential. Plain SAS and Shared Key stay supported, but not recommended. 
 Recommended: Blob access with a User Delegation SAS 
 An Entra ID identity signs the SAS, and the blob client uses it with no account key: 
 DATA(lo_credential) = NEW zcl_az_client_secret_cred( " a Microsoft Entra ID identity 
 iv_client_id = '<client-id>' 
 iv_client_secret = '<client-secret>' 
 iv_tenant_id = '<tenant-id>' ). 
 DATA(lo_udk) = NEW zcl_az_blob_udk_sas( 
 iv_account_name = '<storage-account>' 
 io_credential = lo_credential ). 
 DATA(lo_blob) = lo_udk->create_blob_client( 
 iv_container = '<container>' 
 iv_permissions = 'rl' 
 iv_start = '2026-07-24T00:00:00Z' 
 iv_expiry = '2026-07-25T00:00:00Z' ). 
 DATA(lo_result) = lo_blob->list_blobs( iv_container = '<container>' ). 
 What is included in the first release? 
 Three service clients ship: 
 Storage Blob: list containers and blobs, upload, and download, binary safe. 
 Compute: virtual machines, scale sets, images, and hosts, with actions like start, deallocate, and restart. 
 Resource Graph: run KQL queries, typed result back. 
 DATA(lo_rg) = NEW zcl_az_resourcegraph_client( io_credential = lo_credential ). 
 DATA(lo_result) = lo_rg->query_resources( 
 iv_query = `Resources | project name, type, location | limit 5` 
 it_subscriptions = VALUE #( ( '<subscription-id>' ) ) ). 
 Getting started 
 Developers will need an SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment or S/4HANA Cloud system with ABAP for Cloud Development, a Microsoft Entra ID identity (for example a service principal) with the right Azure RBAC roles, and access to the target Azure resources. Clone and import with abapGit: the code sits under a hierarchy rooted at ` ZABAP_SDK_AZURE `. Assign the root package to the parent package, then activate. 
 The ` ZABAP_AZ_DEMO ` package adds three self contained demo classes, one per service, each an ` if_oo_adt_classrun ` class developers run with F9. Swap in the relevant values and run it; the blob demo shows the whole stack. Real credentials should be kept out of commits. 
 Built with testing in mind 
 The SDK ships with ABAP Unit test methods, all ` RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT ` (no network), plus self skipping integration tests for live verification. Clients accept a test double, so each test checks the exact request on the wire and how a canned response is parsed. Core and every service client are covered. 
 What this means for SAP teams 
 Less boilerplate, faster delivery: Development teams can connect ABAP Cloud applications to Azure services more quickly and spend less time building infrastructure code from scratch. 
 Familiar developer experience: The SDK follows the same concepts used across the official Azure SDK ecosystem. 
 Cloud-ready and compliant: The SDK is ABAP Cloud compliant and designed for SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment and SAP S/4HANA Cloud, making it a natural companion to the classic ABAP SDK for Azure. 
 Secure by default: Microsoft Entra ID is the preferred authentication model, with User Delegation SAS recommended for Azure Storage scenarios. 
 Looking ahead 
 This is just the beginning. The runtime is ready to grow to more Azure services, and which come next depends on community needs. 
 The SDK was created to help ABAP developers and integration teams build secure, maintainable connections between SAP and Azure with less effort. As more teams adopt it, community feedback and real-world business scenarios will help shape future service support and capabilities. 
 If there is an Azure service or integration scenario that matters to your team, we would love to hear from you. Open an issue, start a discussion on GitHub, and help influence the roadmap. 
 Repository: https://github.com/Azure/ABAP-Cloud-SDK-for-Azure

title: Driving Operational Excellence in Waste and Recycling : SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS02
author: SomikSarkar
text:
SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS2 introduces three targeted innovations designed to address critical operational challenges in the Waste & Recycling industry. From AI-powered contract creation to modernized weighbridge operations, this feature pack stack focuses on accuracy, efficiency, and user experience. 
 AI-Assisted Contract Creation in Waste and Recycling 
 Errors in product configurations during contract creation can have a cascading impact on downstream processes such as planning, collections, and billing. This innovation brings artificial intelligence directly into the contract creation process to help waste and recycling customers avoid such errors. 
 What it does: 
 The solution leverages machine learning and intelligent scenario lifecycle management for SAP S/4HANA to recommend the most suitable waste materials based on historical waste contracts. By analyzing patterns in existing contract data, the system suggests material configurations that are consistent with proven combinations, helping to ensure accuracy from the outset. Since majority of the issues are related to an incorrect waste material assignment, the system triggers the AI model to propose the most suitable waste material based on the other customer attributes available. 
 Why it matters: 
 Reduces costly rework caused by incorrect product configurations 
 Prevents issues in downstream processes including planning, waste collection scheduling, and billing 
 Increases operational efficiency 
 This is a significant step in SAP's broader strategy of embedding AI capabilities into industry-specific business processes and application, bringing intelligent automation where it can deliver tangible operational value. 
 Change of Transaction Control for Business Transaction WA15 
 Operational flexibility in managing waste disposal orders is essential, particularly when standard system settings do not align with specific customer requirements. This innovation addresses that gap. 
 What it does: 
 It provides configurable flexibility for customers to add specific rules that override the standard settings maintained in transaction BS22 for waste disposal orders. Specifically, it allows the deletion of waste disposal orders to be governed by settings defined at the individual customer level, rather than being restricted solely by the default system-wide configuration. 
 Why it matters: 
 Empowers customers to define their own business rules with regards to deletion of waste disposal orders. 
 Reduces the need for custom development or workarounds to achieve desired transaction behaviors 
 New SAP Fiori App for Multi-Item Weighing 
 Weighbridge operations are at the heart of waste management logistics. This innovation introduces a new SAP Fiori application with a leaner and lighter interface purpose-built for weighbridge operators handling multi-item weighing scenarios. 
 What it does: 
 The new application supports the main weighing processes through a modern, intuitive user interface: 
 Internal delivery 
 External delivery 
 Internal outbound 
 External outbound 
 Why it matters: 
 Provides a streamlined, responsive user experience that reduces time spent per transaction at the weighbridge 
 Replaces complex legacy interfaces with a modern SAP Fiori design 
 Supports faster processing during peak hours when queue management is critical 
 Mobile compatible, allowing greater flexibility to capture data especially when the operators are on the move within the waste disposal facility. 

 Looking Ahead 
 These three innovations in SAP S/4HANA for Waste and Recycling 2025 FPS02 reflect SAP's continued commitment in making waste management operations smarter, more flexible, and easier to use. By combining AI-driven intelligence in back-office processes, configurable transaction control for operational flexibility, and a modern Fiori-based weighing application for frontline users, SAP is addressing the full spectrum of needs across the waste and recycling value chain. 
 For the latest details and updates, refer to the SAP Roadmap Explorer .

title: Clearing SE16N Buffer After Table Structure Changes
author: Pooja_HM
text:
Introduction 
 While working on custom developments, we often modify database tables after they have already been used in transactions such as SE16N. In one of my recent developments, I increased the length of a field in a custom table. Although the table was activated successfully and the database adjustment was completed, SE16N continued to display the old field length. 
 This blog explains why this behavior occurs and how it can be resolved using a standard SAP program. 

 I created a custom database table ZPOOJ_DB_BLOG_TB in SE11 with three fields. The Email field was initially defined with a length of 5 . 
 Initial Table Definition 
 Custom table with Email field length 5 
 At this stage, the table was activated and some test data was maintained. 
 To allow future enhancements, I changed the Enhancement Category to "Can be Enhanced (Deep)" and activated the table. 
 After that, I used SE16N to maintain table entries. 
 Data Maintenance in SE16N 
 SE16N allowing only 5 characters for Email field 

 As expected, the Email field allowed only five characters. 
 Requirement Change 
 Later, a requirement came in to increase the Email field length from 5 to 25 characters. 
 I modified the corresponding domain in SE11 and activated the changes. 
 Modified Field Length 
 Email field length changed to 25 
 After activation, I adjusted the database table through SE14 to ensure the database structure was updated. 
 To verify the change, I maintained table contents using Utilities → Table Contents . 
 Verification Through Table Contents 
 Email field accepting 25 characters 
 The updated field length was working correctly. 
 Issue Observed 
 However, when I returned to SE16N and tried to create or modify entries, the Email field still allowed only five characters. 
 Issue in SE16N 
 SE16N still showing old field length 
 At first glance, it appeared as though the field length change had not been applied. However, the database table was already updated correctly. 
 The reason for this behavior is that SE16N stores table metadata in its buffer . Since the table was accessed before the modification, SE16N continued to use the buffered information instead of reading the latest table definition. 
 Solution 
 SAP provides a standard report called BALVBUFDEL that clears the ALV buffer information. 
 Execute the report using transaction SE38 . 
 Execute Standard Program BALVBUFDEL 
 Running BALVBUFDEL report 
 After executing the report, return to SE16N and test the table again. 
 Result After Buffer Refresh 
 Email field now accepting 25 characters in SE16N 
 The updated field length is now correctly reflected in SE16N. 

 Conclusion 
 When changes are made to the structure of a database table, such as increasing the length of a field, the changes may not immediately appear in SE16N even though the table has been activated and adjusted successfully. 
 In such situations, the issue is often caused by buffered metadata used by SE16N. Executing the standard SAP report BALVBUFDEL clears the buffer and forces SE16N to read the latest table definition. 
 This simple check can save significant troubleshooting time when table structure changes do not seem to be reflected in SE16N.

title: Building an ATC-Based Transport Release Assistant with AI Code Suggestions in SAP GUI (ECC)?
author: Kishan1
text:
Hi SAP ABAP Community, 
 I'm currently developing a custom ABAP tool and would appreciate feedback from experienced SAP developers on whether this solution is useful, whether similar functionality already exists in SAP ECC, and whether my proposed UI architecture is technically feasible. 
 Background 
 I've heard that in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition, certain development and transport processes can enforce ATC checks before changes are released or deployed. 
 This made me wonder: 
 Is there any standard functionality in SAP ECC / SAP GUI that prevents a transport request from being released until specific ATC or Code Inspector findings are resolved? 
 If such functionality already exists, I'd like to understand it before continuing with a custom solution. 
 What I've developed so far 
 I'm currently testing this on an SAP_BASIS 740 system using SAP GUI. 
 My prototype can: 
 Read an ABAP program and check whether it has opted in for review. 
 Execute Code Inspector checks programmatically using ABAP classes. 
 Extract findings, including severity, check description, source line, and surrounding source-code context. 
 Store the execution results in custom database tables (ZOKG_LOG_HDR and ZOKG_LOG_ITEM). 
 Identify a program with findings and automatically open it in the standard SE38 ABAP Editor in Change mode. 
 Display a separate AI Code Review screen using CL_GUI_CUSTOM_CONTAINER and CL_GUI_TEXTEDIT, with a Copy Code button. 
 Currently, the AI code is sample output. Integration with an LLM to generate actual corrections is planned. 
 The longer-term goal is to integrate this with the CTS transport-release process using IF_EX_CTS_REQUEST_CHECK~CHECK_BEFORE_RELEASE, so that relevant findings can be reviewed before releasing a transport request. 
 Current limitation: Two SAP GUI sessions 
 At present, my tool opens two separate SAP GUI sessions: 
 Session 1: The actual SE38 ABAP Editor, with the target program opened in Change mode. 
 Session 2: My custom AI review screen displaying suggested code. 
 This works, but I would prefer to provide the entire review experience within the SE38 window. 
 What I want to achieve 
 When my tool opens a program in SE38, I would like a dialog box to open automatically within that same SAP GUI session. 
 The dialog would contain a tabstrip with two tabs: 
 Tab 1 — AI Suggested Code 
 Display the AI-generated corrected ABAP code in a read-only editor, with an option to copy the suggested code. The developer can review the suggestion and manually apply the changes in SE38. 
 Tab 2 — ATC / Code Inspector Findings 
 Display the findings for the current program, including severity, description, line number, and relevant source-code context. 
 I would also like to add a button to the SE38 toolbar, such as AI / ATC Review. 
 The expected behavior would be: 
 The review dialog opens automatically when the program is opened through my tool. 
 The developer can close the dialog and continue working in SE38. 
 The SE38 editor remains open. 
 The developer can click the AI / ATC Review button at any time to reopen the dialog. 
 My technical questions 
 Existing functionality: Does SAP ECC already provide a standard ATC or Code Inspector-based transport-release gate? Are there established alternatives such as CTS checks or transport quality gates? 
 SE38 enhancement: Is there any supported BAdI, customer exit, enhancement point, or API that allows a custom dialog and toolbar button to be integrated into the standard SE38 ABAP Editor? 
 GUI session handling: Since RS_TOOL_ACCESS with IN_NEW_WINDOW = 'X' opens the editor in another SAP GUI session, is there a supported way to initialize and reopen a custom dialog from within that editor session? 
 Architecture: Would you recommend extending the standard SE38 interface, developing a custom editor/review transaction, or keeping the current two-session approach? 
 Project value: Do you think a tool combining pre-release ATC checks, source-code context, AI suggestions, and developer-controlled corrections would be useful in an ECC development environment? 
 I'm trying to keep the implementation maintainable and avoid modifications to SAP standard objects. 
 I'd appreciate any suggestions, relevant SAP documentation, existing tools, or alternative approaches. 
 Thanks in advance!

title: Hong Kong PROFITS TAX COMPUTATION Depreciation Allowances
author: ChristopherWan
text:
All group company codes are located in Hong Kong. Please refer to the detailed fixed-asset tax depreciation requirements below, based on Hong Kong Profits Tax treatment. 
 Please advise on the standard SAP approach to fulfil these requirements. 
 Tax depreciation of fixed assets Tax depreciation allowances / deductions are available for capital expenditure incurred on the construction of buildings or structures and in the provision of machinery and plant for trade or business purposes, as follows: 
 1. Industrial buildings and structures: An initial allowance of 20%, in addition to an annual allowance of 4%, of the cost of construction or cost of purchase from a developer is granted for an industrial building or structure occupied for the purpose of a qualifying trade. Provision is made for balancing allowance or charge in the year of assessment in which the building is disposed of to adjust the written-down value of the building to the disposal price. Balancing charges are restricted to the total of initial and annual allowances previously given. 
 2. Commercial buildings and structures: An annual allowance of 4% of the capital expenditure incurred on the construction is applicable. A balancing allowance or charge applies upon disposal. Balancing charges are restricted to the total annual allowances previously given. 
 3. Plant and machinery: An initial allowance of 60% of the capital expenditure on plant and machinery is given for the year of assessment during the basis period in which the expenditure is incurred. An annual allowance is also given for depreciation at three prescribed rates on the reducing value of each of the three depreciation rate ‘pools’. The three prescribed rates are 10%, 20%, and 30%, and the reducing value of each of the three depreciation rate pools is original cost less initial and annual allowances and sales proceeds. Provision is made for balancing charges when plant and machinery within one of the three depreciation rate pools is sold or disposed of and the reducing value of that pool is less than the sale price, which is capped at the original amount incurred in the pool. In addition, balancing allowances or charges may be applicable upon cessation of business. Otherwise, sales proceeds are deducted in calculating the reducing value on which the annual allowance is calculated.

title: IBOP - From Sub-Item Adjustments to Main-Item Mastery: Unlocking Alternative-Based Confirmations!
author: Shishira_Shastri_H
text:
If you haven't already, have a look at our previous blogs in this series to see how Interactive Backorder Processing (IBOP) evolved from its initial 2023 FPS03 launch to the constraint-busting Unrestricted Checks in 2025 FPS0 and the Rounding Capabilities , System Proposals , etc., in 2025 FPS1. 
 Now, with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS2 , we are taking another massive leap forward! This release introduces full support for Alternative-Based Confirmation (ABC) Main Items directly within your interactive worklist, alongside powerful new extensibility options. 
 Why ABC in Interactive BOP? 

 Imagine you are an Order Fulfillment Specialist dealing with an urgent supply shortage for a high-value sales order. In standard processing, if the primary plant or storage location is out of stock, your order gets backordered or delayed. 
 Alternative-Based Confirmation (ABC) acts as an automated fallback mechanism during ATP checks to solve this exact problem by dynamically scouting alternative plants, storage locations, or substitute products. 
 In earlier releases, IBOP only allowed users to review and tweak existing ABC sub-items after they were already generated. If you wanted to re-evaluate the main item to trigger fresh alternatives, you couldn't do it directly within the interactive app. 2025 FPS2 changes the game entirely! 
 2025 FPS2 Release Highlights 
 1. Full Integration of ABC Main Items & Hierarchy Tree View 
 Starting with 2025 FPS2, you can load ABC Main Items into your IBOP worklist right from the requirement selection wizard by enabling the "Include Main Item" option or directly via the Select Option Tool by defining appropriate conditions. 
 Hierarchical Tree View: Requirements are loaded into a clear, intuitive tree structure showing the parent main item alongside its child sub-items. 
 Hierarchy View 
 Flexible Worklist Control: You can now perform mass recheck actions ( Improve , Redistribute , Lose ) at the main-item level or target specific sub-items individually. 
 Requirement Selection: Include ABC Main Item 
 2. Dynamic Sub-Item Generation & Mass Rechecks 
 When you trigger a recheck on an ABC main item, the system automatically evaluates your maintained alternative determination configurations. 
 Automated Sourcing: The ATP check evaluates available alternatives and automatically generates a new set of delta sub-items - adding new alternative sourcing lines, updating existing ones, or removing obsolete lines. 
 Third-Party Order Processing (TPOP) Support: The release also supports main-item rechecks in partial TPOP scenarios, where customer orders are redirected to external vendors or internal sourcing plants when local inventory is unavailable. 
 TPOP Sub-item distinguished from a Normal item 
 What Partial TPOP with Main-Item Rechecks Means ? 
 Dynamic Sourcing Integration: When an order cannot be fulfilled from local warehouse stock, an ATP check on the ABC main item can determine a third-party vendor (TPOP) as an alternative sourcing line. 
 Rechecking Main Items: In IBOP, fulfillment specialists can now recheck the main item of an order that involves partial TPOP, allowing the system to re-evaluate vendor confirmations and local stock simultaneously. 
 Purchase Order (PO) Confirmations: If a TPOP requirement already has active Purchase Order confirmations from a vendor, those quantities are automatically subtracted from the open requested and confirmed amounts before the recheck is executed. 
 3. Enhanced Extensibility: BAdI for Fixed Date & Quantity (FIXMG) 
 To give businesses maximum flexibility, 2025 FPS2 introduces a dedicated Business Add-In (BAdI) enhancement point: ATP_IBOP_ENHANCE_REQUIREMENTS. 
 Automated Confirmation Protection: Key Users / Developers can now implement custom business logic to automatically set or update the Fixed Date and Quantity (FIXMG) indicator for schedule lines following an ATP recheck. 
 Custom Governance: This ensures your automated rules can lock in vital confirmations based on your organization's unique operational priorities. 
 The Verdict 
 The 2025 FPS2 release bridges the gap between intelligent automated sourcing and interactive manual control. By combining ABC main-item evaluation with custom BAdI extensibility , Interactive Backorder Processing gives fulfillment specialists the ultimate control to maximize confirmations and keep customers happy, even in the toughest supply chain bottlenecks! 
 The journey doesn't stop here - keep an eye out for upcoming features on the horizon, from ODL integration to advanced alternative determinations , designed to make your fulfillment operations even smarter. Stay tuned! 
 For more information, please refer to the SAP Help: 2025FPS2 
 Kind regards, 
 Shishira Shastri H 
 Co-authored by: @MaitriMohan

title: Evolution of Classic Operations Control Center towards Autonomous Operations Control Center
author: Robin_Haettich
text:
Previous articles have described the Operations Control Center (OCC) as an integral part of SAP’s best practice operational model for IT organizations. Today more than ever before, the OCC as embedded in SAP’s Customer Center of Expertise (CCOE) best practice and master class, is a pillar of SAP’s Clean Core recommendation, and serves as the customers’ organizational unit integral to collaborating with their operations partners (i.e. SAP Enterprise Cloud Services in SAP RISE). 
 Additional references of more advanced topics and applications relevant in and for the Operations Control Center have been outlined in part 1 (Robotic Process Automation), part 2 (Conversational Artificial Intelligence), part 3 (Intelligent Operations Analytics), part 4 (Simplified Process Monitoring), and part 5 (Intelligent Usage of Data and Information) of previous article series. 
 The evolution of this essential concept and practice is the OCC’s capabilities to support SAP’s path towards Autonomous Enterprise, embracing Autonomous Operations or Autonomous Application Lifecycle Management (ALM). Technically, this is based on the SAP Integrated Toolchain or Agent-led Toolchain or equivalent software products and tools. This article summarizes a few important dimensions and capabilities of this evolution towards the Autonomous Operations Control Center. 
 Organizational Embedding of Modern Operations Control Center‎s 
 In context of an Operations Control Center, IT organizations collect data and provide information (Detection, Observability) and act on this information (Correction, Improvement) - to govern and manage the system and solution landscape of the enterprise architecture. This includes not only IT infrastructure, systems, components - what the OCC refers to as system landscape - but encompasses business scenarios, processes, components - what the OCC refers to as solution landscape. 

 Relevance in SAP Customer Center of Expertise 
 The Operations Control Center is one of the centerpieces of the Customer Center of Expertise. The Customer Center of Expertise (CCOE) is SAP's best practice organizational operating model. More specifically, the Customer COEs act as collaboration hubs across IT and lines of business, with a mission to provide transparency and efficiency of implementation, innovation, operation, and quality of business processes and systems related to SAP software solutions and services. The CCOE is organized around two control centers, the OCC (Run Operations) and the ALM team or teams (Build Operations). 

 I n doing so, the CCOE enables IT service and cost excellence by improving customer satisfaction and reducing the total cost of ownership and acts as an enabler for continuous innovation. Especially interesting in modern IT organizations is the CCOE's as well as for Run Operation the OCC's governance between itself and external stakeholders such as service providers and operations partners. 
 Relevance in SAP RISE 
 The Operations Control Center serves as the customer entity which establishes and executes communication and collaboration with operations partners, among them SAP ECS/CAS in a RISE context. 
 As mentioned in the last paragraph, the OCC acts as the interface between SAP and the customer's organization, organizationally, procedurally, and technically. The latter is facilitated by SAP’s Agent-led, integrated toolchain, which serves as technical interface between the Customer OCC and ITSM processes in general and SAP in its roles as product support, service delivery, and service provider. 

 SAP Cloud ALM for service is the component within the Agent-led, integrated toolchain which serves as the technical component facilitating this ITSM integration with SAP. Several use cases are supported for collaborative Event Management, Incident Management, Root Cause Analysis, and Service Management. 
 Relevance in SAP Clean Core 
 The Operations Control Center supports customers’ Clean Core compliance. SAP Clean Core is a strategic framework and set of guiding principles designed to help organizations keep their SAP-centric system and solution landscape agile, cost-effective, and innovation-ready. At its essence, Clean Core means minimizing invasive customizations within the core by extending functionality through compliant, decoupled mechanisms instead. 
 The 5th dimensions of Clean Core, Operations, is realized as Operations Control Center. Any dimension is considered "clean" when best practices, methodologies, and tools are effectively applied, and for the technical implementation SAP recommends again the Agent-led, integrated toolchain. 

 Process Capabilities of Modern Operations Control Centers 
 The Operations Control Center needs to understand how its users and its customers, the business end-users, are feeling about the system and solution landscape. Following best practice, it is responsible at least for the following IT processes: 
 Event Management : identify issues and address immediately (Detect-to-Correct – Fix Pace ), 
 Continuous Improvement : assess and progress provided solutions and improved services (Assess to Deploy – Enhancement Pace ). 
 As we have seen, the Operations Control Center relies on a toolchain for documentation, transformation, monitoring, alerting, analysis, reporting, visualization and automation, including but not limited to the SAP Agent-led, integrated toolchain products below. 
 The Operation Control Center utilizes SAP LeanIX, Signavio, and Cloud ALM and/or equivalent software to establish monitoring and event management as well as analytics and continuous improvement. Moreover, information visualization and process automation software is essential in the Operate phase. 

 Automation and AI in Modern Operations Control Centers 
 Autonomous Event Management 
 Classic Detect to Correct procedures and their past evolutions have been described in previous articles (see section Further Reading). Modern Event Management uses SAP and non-SAP tooling to automate detection as well as correction, adding machine learning, generative AI, and agentic AI wherever applicable and beneficial. SAP’s main product for this capability is SAP Cloud ALM for Operations (including its inbound and outbound interfaces). The benefits are obvious and have been elaborated in previous articles, in a nutshell they include establishing observability across a changing system and solution landscape, resolving issues efficiently and repetitively, and providing the groundwork for continuous improvement. 
 Modern Detect to Correct procedures evolve by utilizing AI Agents and Assistants overtaking previous manual steps. 

 In the above example, the alert creation (which was always automated), the impact analysis, the operating procedure (including root cause analysis and approved resolution steps) are all automated and executed by AI Agents or OCC Operobots . The human OCC Operators are governing, approving, and acting as human in the loop . 
 Autonomous Continuous Improvement 
 Classic Continuous Improvement procedures and their past evolutions have been described in previous articles (see section Further Reading). Modern Continuous Improvement uses SAP and non-SAP tooling to automate assessment and identification of improvement candidates, as well as the recommendation of how to realize these potentials, adding generative AI and and agentic AI wherever applicable and beneficial. SAP’s main product for this capability is SAP Cloud ALM for Service (including its inbound and outbound interfaces). 
 Modern Continuous Improvement procedures evolve by utilizing AI Agents and Assistants as well, which as in the case or Event Management, complement or replace previous manual steps. 

 I n the above example, the improvement candidate identification (which was always supported by semi-automation in a well-run OCC), benefit and priority analysis, as well as decision making and even implementation tasks of the selected candidate are all automated by utilizing corresponding AI Agents. The human OCC Operators – together with the Continuous Improvement leads and Enterprise Architects - are governing, approving, and acting as human in the loop . 
 Technical Foundation for Autonomous Operations Control Center 
 In an SAP-centric Operations Control Center, SAP Cloud ALM and/or equivalent software will support AI-supported operations. With Joule support, SAP Cloud ALM already started its journey towards autonomous operations and announced to continuously improve its agentic capabilities moving forward. 

 Agents and Assistants for Detect to Correct 
 An AI/Agent-supported Event Management could look like the below. 

 I n this example, AI assistants and agents streamline workflows, (semi-)automate analyses and resolutions, and deliver connected intelligence across the Detect-to-Correct process across SAP and non-SAP system and solution landscapes. Conversational UIs in state-of-the-art Run Operations software provide access to contextual insights and task guidance directly where OCC operators do their jobs. 
 In SAP Cloud ALM for example, Joule will present relevant information about an issue (detected as event or events). The detection, the analysis, and resolution tasks Operators did manually based on Guided Procedures are now semi- or even fully automatable. 
 In SAP Cloud ALM, Joule with SAP Cloud ALM is already available for eligible SAP Cloud ALM customers. This initial release delivers a conversational AI assistant embedded within SAP Cloud ALM, helping users navigate the application and find the information they need — faster and more intuitively ( ALM Alert Resolution Agent and ALM Dashboard Generation Agent ). 
 Agents and Assistants for Identify to Improve 
 An AI/Agent-supported Continuous Improvement could look like the below. 

 In this example, AI assistants and agents prepare decisions, streamline initiatives and projects, and deliver connected intelligence across the Identify-to-Improve process across SAP and non-SAP system and solution landscapes. 
 Take SAP Cloud ALM example, Joule will support Issues and Action Management by summarizing information on issues, filtering the summary and exporting it to various outputs (to possibly be consumed by other task automation agents). Moreover, SAP Cloud ALM's AI Assistance for Innovation Adoption creates Continuous Improvement recommendations together with issues and recommended actions for the lines of business (LOB) and the simplification items for the organization's enterprise architects. If the implementation of the improvement candidate requires a project, SAP Cloud ALM for Implementation offers Joule support for project management, team management, change management, including test management. 
 In SAP Cloud ALM, the initial release already delivers Agents creating recommendations as well as managing issues and actions ( Evolution Readiness Agent and Issue and Actions ). 
 As a result, Joule lowers risk and cost by keeping the lights on, i.e. by reducing operational friction and improving cross-team collaboration, so core business processes run more effectively. Operators gain improved navigation as well as measurable insight, enabling a path towards agentic OCC scenarios with confidence. In addition, Joule increases the return on investment by supporting the continuous identification and selection of innovation items.

title: UDV Event-Based Triggering
author: OferOz
text:
SAP Business One 10.0 FP 2608 brings a nice enhancement to User-Defined Values (UDV): a new way to trigger a formula based on events. 
 If you've worked with UDV formulas ( mathematical or logical ), you know that for a formula to run automatically, you need to define a trigger – a field on the form that, when changed by the user, activates the formula and populates the target field. 
 This works well in many cases. But what if you want the formula to run when the user clicks ‘Add’ or ‘Update’, rather than when a specific field changes? Before FP 2608, that wasn't possible. 
 FP 2608 introduces two new triggering options: 
 - On events – the formula runs automatically when the document is Added or Updated. No trigger field needed. 
 - On field changes or events – a combined mode: the formula runs both when a trigger field changes or when the document is Added or Updated. 

 The existing trigger on field change only is still available. 
 Example: a ssume you have a UDF called 'Last Modified By' on a sales order, and you want it to always store the name of the user who last saved the document. With the new events option, the formula simply runs on every Add or Update. 
 For more details, refer to the online help . 
 This is a small but impactful change - it lets UDV formulas respond to the most natural user action: adding or saving a document.

title: Managing Parent-Child Hierarchies in SAC: One Small Update That Simplifies Everything
author: Tano_B
text:
Introduction 
 Every once in a while SAP delivers a feature that doesn't make it into keynotes or release highlights. Yet some of these smaller improvements can have a surprisingly large impact on day-to-day development. 
 One such improvement recently appeared in SAC hierarchy loading. While it may look like a minor technical change, it removes one of the reasons why hierarchy loads often required additional preprocessing, filtering logic, and cleanup workarounds. 

 The Old Behavior 
 Imagine your dimension has members, that are not completely assigned to the hierarchy. In this example, there are Marketing CostCenters assigned to a Marketing Node, while the Production (P_...) CostCenters are not assigned to the hierarchy: 

 Member ID Parent 
 M_A Marketing 
 M_B Marketing 
 M_C Marketing 
 P_A NULL 
 P_B NULL 
 P_C NULL 
 Marketing 
 With the traditional SAC load behavior, members without a parent assignment were automatically placed below <root>. 
 As a result, the loaded hierarchy looked like this: 

 This behavior was often undesirable. 
 The Production cost centers were valid dimension members, but they were not intended to be part of the Marketing hierarchy. Nevertheless, SAC automatically added them as root nodes because no parent assignment was provided. 
 For dimensions with multiple hierarchies, this quickly became a challenge. Every hierarchy would suddenly contain large numbers of unrelated members below <root>, making the hierarchy difficult to maintain and more difficult for business users to navigate. 
 Because of this, a common recommendation emerged: 
 Load all dimension members first. 
 Load each hierarchy separately. 
 Restrict every hierarchy load to the members that actually belong to that hierarchy. 
 While effective, this approach introduced additional data flows, transformations, and maintenance effort solely to avoid unwanted <root> assignments. 

 The New Behavior 
 Now SAC can distinguish between three fundamentally different scenarios: 
 assigned to a parent node 
 assigned to <root> (blank / empty string) 
 not assigned to the hierarchy (NULL ) 
 Using the same example, the hierarchy load can now provide NULL for members that should be excluded from the hierarchy: 

 The Production cost centers remain valid dimension members, but they are no longer added to the hierarchy: 

 This seemingly small change eliminates one of the main reasons why hierarchies had to be loaded separately in the first place. 
 If you are using Seamless Planning with Datasphere or expose SAC master data through the Data Provisioning Agent (DPA), this enhancement becomes even more valuable. 
 Instead of maintaining hierarchy assignments separately, you can use the existing dimension members as the starting point and simply join them with the hierarchy source. Members without a matching hierarchy assignment can be loaded with a NULL parent value and are automatically removed from the hierarchy: 
 SQL Example: Exposed Dimension Members in Datasphere with Hierarchy Join 
 This makes it much easier to keep hierarchies synchronized with the actual set of active members and to clean up obsolete hierarchy assignments. 
 For the first time, hierarchy loads can be used not only to create or change hierarchy relationships, but also to remove them! 

 Impact on Existing Hierarchy Workarounds 
 In my previous blog post , I described one of the key limitations of SAC hierarchy loading: members could not truly leave a hierarchy through the load process. When a parent assignment was cleared, SAC interpreted the record as a root member and placed it below <root> instead. 
 However, this limitation had implications far beyond hierarchy cleanup. 
 Because SAC treated missing parent assignments as <root>, a common recommendation emerged for dimensions with multiple hierarchies: load the master data first and maintain each hierarchy separately. Otherwise, members that did not belong to a specific hierarchy would still appear in that hierarchy as root nodes. 
 As a consequence, additional filtering logic, separate hierarchy loads, and custom cleanup procedures became common implementation patterns. 
 With the new NULL handling, many of these workarounds are no longer required. 
 A NULL parent assignment now explicitly removes the hierarchy relationship while keeping the member itself in the dimension. Members that do not belong to a hierarchy no longer have to be excluded from the load process entirely. Instead, they can simply be loaded with a NULL parent value. 
 The benefit is especially visible when using Seamless Planning or exposing SAC dimensions through the Data Provisioning Agent (DPA). In these scenarios, existing SAC members can be used as the starting point, joined with the hierarchy source, and loaded back into SAC. Members without a matching hierarchy assignment simply receive a NULL parent value and are removed from the hierarchy automatically. 

 Conclusion 
 For many years, the behavior of SAC hierarchy loads shaped common implementation practices. Separate hierarchy loads, additional filtering logic, and hierarchy cleanup workarounds were often necessary to avoid unwanted <root> assignments. 
 With the introduction of NULL-based hierarchy removal, SAC now provides a clear distinction between: 
 a member assigned to a parent node 
 a member assigned to <root> 
 a member that does not belong to the hierarchy at all 
 This seemingly small enhancement not only solves one of the limitations discussed in my previous blog post. It also simplifies the loading of dimensions with multiple hierarchies and reduces the need for several long-standing implementation workarounds. 
 No keynote. No release highlight. Just a small change that quietly removes one of the longest-standing pain points in SAC hierarchy loading.

title: Official Document Numbers (ODN) now replicated in Central Finance
author: christian_seelinger
text:
As tax authorities worldwide tighten their grip on digital reporting, the document number on an invoice is no longer just an internal reference — it is a legally binding identifier that must flow accurately through every system in your landscape. SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS02 closes a critical gap for Central Finance customers by introducing Official Document Number (ODN) replication . 
 What Is an Official Document Number? 
 An Official Document Number (ODN) is a unique identifier that companies are legally required to assign to specific business documents — invoices, credit notes, and similar records — in accordance with rules set by government authorities. The format, length, and structure of an ODN vary by country and are strictly defined by regulators. 
 Until recently, SAP stored ODNs in standard reference fields on the accounting document (such as BKPF-XBLNR ). These fields were too short for some countries' requirements, and customers frequently repurposed them for other business data. The ODN framework (available since S/4HANA 1709) introduced a dedicated storage structure — table GSLOG_LFD — with sufficient length, multi-value support per document, and a clear separation from other reference fields. 
 The Central Finance Challenge 
 Central Finance (CFIN) lets organizations replicate financial postings from one or more source ERP systems (S/4HANA or ECC) into a central S/4HANA hub — without replacing the source systems. This is a popular path for harmonizing statutory reporting while keeping existing operations running. 
 The challenge: when a document is replicated from source to Central Finance, it gets a new FI document number in the target system. Without additional handling, the ODN assigned in the source would be lost — leaving Central Finance with legally incomplete documents. 
 ⚠️ POLAND / KSeF DEADLINE 
 Poland's mandatory KSeF e-invoicing regime requires every invoice to carry a government-issued KSeF number. For companies running Central Finance, this number must be present in the CFIN system for statutory reporting — making ODN replication a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have. 
 How ODN Replication Works 
 SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS02 introduces native ODN replication as part of the Central Finance integration. The solution covers two main scenarios: 

 🔄 Scenario 1 — Clearing Transfer (AP/AR Invoices) 
 AP/AR invoices — FI, SD billing, and MM — are posted in the source system where the ODN is assigned (for example, a KSeF number received from the Polish government via DRC e-invoicing). During replication to Central Finance, the ODN is carried across and persisted in GSLOG_LFD against the new CFIN FI document key, while traceability to the original source document number is maintained. 
 A document header can carry multiple ODNs — for example, a Poland invoice may hold both an individual KSeF number and a collective KSeF reference. All are replicated. 

 💳 Scenario 2 — Central Payment 
 Invoices are posted in the source; the actual payment and clearing documents are created directly in Central Finance. For Poland, no ODN is currently legally required on the payment/clearing document itself. If a future jurisdiction mandates it, the ODN framework in CFIN is ready to assign one centrally. 
 Preservation vs. Assignment 
 The solution operates in two modes depending on configuration and legal requirement: 
 Preservation mode: The source ODN is validated and stored in CFIN unchanged. Target-side ODN generation is disabled for replicated documents to prevent the source number from being overwritten. 
 Assignment mode: If a document is created natively in CFIN (for example, a central payment) and a country requires an ODN, CFIN assigns one using its own ODN framework configuration and number ranges. 
 Source Coverage 
 S/4HANA source: ODNs are read from GSLOG_LFD ( RECORD_TYPE = 'ODN' ) for document types ADH (FI header), BDH (SD billing header), and IDH (MM invoice header). All ODN fields — including timestamps and ODN type — are replicated unchanged. 
 ECC source: The ODN framework does not exist in ECC; country- or customer-specific extraction logic maps values into the CFIN ODN storage. 
 Initial load: Existing FI header ODN data can be back-filled together with the FI document initial load. 
 Why It Matters for Business 
 Centralised compliance: If your statutory reporting runs out of Central Finance, ODNs flow automatically — no manual reconciliation between systems. 
 Future-proof architecture: The ODN framework is country-agnostic by design. As more jurisdictions introduce mandatory document numbering, replication in Central Finance will be ready. 
 Minimal disruption: Replicated ODN data is stored in the same database table used natively by the ODN framework ( GSLOG_LFD ). Consuming applications and statutory reports in Central Finance require little to no adjustment. 
 Configuration safeguards: ODN number generation in Central Finance is disabled for replicated documents through customer configuration settings (by company code, document type, and further restrictions), preventing replicated numbers from being overwritten. 
 Availability 

 Get Ready for Poland — and What Comes Next 
 If your organisation uses Central Finance and operates in Poland, the time to plan is now. Here is a practical checklist to get started: 
 Verify that DRC e-invoicing is configured in your source systems to receive KSeF numbers from the Polish government. 
 Review ODN generation settings in Central Finance for replicated company codes and document types to prevent conflicts. 
 Scope the initial load for any existing documents that need to be back-filled before the 2026 reporting deadline. 
 For other countries using the ODN framework (Israel, Slovenia, Vietnam) or regions anticipating future mandates — no architectural rework is required ; coverage can be extended incrementally. 
 For more information, visit the SAP Help Portal or reach out to your SAP account team.

title: The Next Chapter in Spend Management: AI Innovations Across SAP Ariba, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP Concur
author: Baber Farooq
text:
Last week at SAP Connect, SAP introduced new capabilities and partner innovations across SAP Ariba, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP Concur that help organizations turn spend insights into faster, better-informed decisions. 
 SAP Connect in 2026: Advancing the Autonomous Enterprise 

 Read the innovation news guide 

 Procurement leaders operate in a very different environment than they did just a few years ago. Beyond cost and compliance, they must now strengthen resilience, manage supplier risk, support workforce strategies, and help businesses respond faster to changing market conditions. 

 Yet, many of the systems supporting these responsibilities remain disconnected. Supplier intelligence lives in one place, workforce information in another, and spend data often requires significant preparation before it can drive decisions. 

 At SAP Connect, we announced a series of innovations across the SAP Ariba, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP Concur portfolios designed to help organizations address those challenges: new AI assistants for spend analysis and contingent workforce management, embedded supplier risk intelligence through a new partnership with Moody’s, a new solution extension with ORO Labs that orchestrates procurement across complex enterprise landscapes, and new SAP Concur capabilities that simplify high-volume administrative work. 

 Together, these innovations point to a broader shift toward Autonomous Spend Management , a domain within the SAP Autonomous Suite . AI connects information, insights, and execution, while people remain in control of the decisions that matter most. 

 Better spend decisions start with better visibility 

 Many procurement organizations still struggle to turn spend data into actionable insight quickly enough to support decision-making. 

 According to the 2026 Economist Enterprise report, Procurement at a Crossroads: From Optimism to Realism , sponsored by SAP, digital transformation is now the top strategic priority for procurement over the next 18 months, and improving spend analytics is one of its biggest drivers, cited by 53% of executives. These findings reflect growing pressure to improve decision-making and business impact. 

 Earlier this month, SAP announced the availability of SAP Ariba Spend Analysis and Insights , giving organizations a new way to bring together spend data across SAP Ariba, SAP Fieldglass, SAP Concur, SAP Cloud ERP, and other systems into a single foundation for analysis and action. 

 Building on that foundation, we announced the new Spend Analytics Assistant at SAP Connect. Planned for general availability in Q1 2027, it helps procurement teams identify opportunities for cost savings, compliance, supplier consolidation, and risk mitigation. Rather than searching through reports, teams see highlighted areas that merit attention, along with supporting context to help them prioritize and act, so they spend more time on decisions and less on data preparation. 

 Bringing supplier risk into everyday decisions 

 Supplier risk is now a strategic concern across every industry, yet risk data often remains disconnected from the sourcing and purchasing decisions where it matters most. 

 At SAP Connect, we also announced a new partnership with Moody’s that embeds supplier risk monitoring directly into SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance . By bringing financial health, operational risk, and regulatory status into the same environment where supplier performance and relationship data are managed, procurement teams can evaluate risk as part of everyday decision-making rather than periodic reviews. 

 The partnership also strengthens the foundation for AI-powered procurement. When risk information is embedded directly within procurement workflows, it becomes part of the business context used to help identify emerging issues and support earlier intervention. This gives teams a more complete view of supplier relationships and greater ability to respond before potential disruptions affect operations. 

 General availability is planned for Q4 2026. 

 Connecting procurement across complex enterprise landscapes 

 The disconnection that slows procurement decisions often extends beyond data; it also shows up across the systems themselves. For many organizations, procurement unfolds across a mix of SAP and third-party applications, each supporting different parts of the process. Coordinating work across that kind of landscape, without disrupting the systems teams already rely on, can be one of modern procurement’s more persistent challenges. 

 To solve this, SAP announced a new solution extension developed with ORO Labs: SAP Ariba Procurement Orchestration by ORO Labs. It provides a purpose-built orchestration layer that connects procurement experiences, workflows, and systems across complex environments spanning both SAP and third-party applications. 

 For employees, this means a more unified experience and a simpler way to initiate and navigate procurement work. Low-code/no-code workflows let teams adapt processes as business requirements and policies change, without disrupting underlying systems. Organizations can also apply agentic AI within these workflows while preserving the controls, approvals, and human oversight that enterprise operations depend on. 

 The solution extension works alongside Joule Work, with Joule Work serving as the primary engagement layer. General availability is planned for November 2026. 

 Making external workforce management more proactive 

 For many organizations, contingent workers have become an essential part of how they scale skills, execute projects, and adapt to changing business needs. Managing those workers, however, often requires coordination across procurement, HR, hiring managers, suppliers, and compliance teams. 

 We also announced the new Contingent Workforce Assistant, designed to bring greater visibility to that process. Planned for general availability in Q4 2026, the assistant helps organizations manage the contingent worker life cycle by surfacing issues such as onboarding delays, pending approvals, compliance requirements, and other exceptions before they affect assignments. By bringing relevant information into a single experience, teams can address issues earlier while maintaining governance and auditability. 

 This proactive approach addresses one of the persistent challenges in workforce management: identifying issues early enough to act before they become operational problems. 

 Simplifying travel and expense management through targeted automation 

 Not every productivity challenge in spend management requires a major transformation initiative. 

 In many organizations, the greatest source of friction in travel and expense management comes from routine administrative work, such as retrieving receipts, locating invoice images, preparing audit documentation, and reviewing user permissions. Individually small, these tasks collectively consume significant time across finance, audit, compliance, and expense management teams. 

 To address this, SAP Concur announced new additions to SAP Micro-App Hub . Building on capabilities already used to support tax, audit, compliance, and reporting, SAP plans to introduce new micro-apps that help organizations export employee expense information, simplify access-governance reviews, and retrieve vendor invoice documentation in bulk. 

 The approach is intentionally practical: rather than redesigning entire processes, the micro-apps target specific operational pain points. Customer adoption of the existing micro-apps points to strong demand for this focused automation. 

 Additional micro-apps are planned for general availability in Q4 2026. 

 Turning spend intelligence into action 

 Most organizations have plenty of spend data. The persistent challenge is turning that information into timely decisions and meaningful business outcomes. 

 The innovations announced this year at SAP Connect address that challenge from multiple angles, improving visibility into spend, bringing risk intelligence closer to procurement decisions, connecting procurement processes across complex enterprise landscapes, improving external workforce management, and reducing administrative effort across travel and expense. 

 Better decisions require better visibility, stronger context, and fewer barriers between identifying an issue and responding to it. This is the goal of Autonomous Spend Management: applying agentic AI across every spend process so disconnected workflows operate as one intelligent, governed system. 

 This matters more as procurement takes on a larger role in driving resilience, growth, and business performance. For organizations that can identify opportunities faster, respond to risk earlier, and spend less time on manual coordination, spend becomes a source of advantage rather than a cost to control. 

 Baber Farooq is chief marketing officer for Spend Management at SAP.

title: SAP Advances Finance Operations with Embedded Payments, New Consolidation Capabilities, and Expanded AI
author: David Imbert
text:
New innovations in payments, enterprise performance management, and AI automation help finance teams move quickly from insight to execution while maintaining governance and control. 
 SAP Connect in 2026: Advancing the Autonomous Enterprise 

 Read the innovation news guide 

 Finance leaders today are expected to do far more than report results. They’re expected to shape business outcomes, guide decisions, and respond quickly to change. Yet many finance processes still operate in isolation rather than in concert. Invoice approval and payment execution happen in separate places. 

 Planning, consolidation, and reporting often rely on separate systems and workflows. And governance often misses critical information by operating in a silo. The result is delays between identifying an issue, making a decision, and taking action. 

 This year at SAP Connect, SAP announced new capabilities designed to help close those gaps. These include SAP Pay , a new payment service embedded in SAP Cloud ERP; SAP Enterprise Financial Consolidation, a new addition to SAP’s enterprise performance management portfolio; and an expanded set of Joule Assistants that bring AI-powered support to finance, governance, and compliance processes. 

 While each innovation addresses a different challenge, they share a common objective. Finance teams should spend less time moving information between systems and more time acting on insights. 

 Embedding payments into finance operations 

 One of the most persistent sources of friction in finance is the payment process itself. 

 An invoice may be approved in the ERP system, but completing the payment often still involves banking portals, payment files, middleware, and reconciliation activities. Each additional handoff introduces complexity and can slow execution. 

 SAP Pay is designed to simplify that process by embedding payment execution directly into SAP Cloud ERP . When an invoice is approved, payment and reconciliation can occur within the same workflow and the same business context. 

 The launch also marks SAP’s entry into payment services through Tereina , a wholly owned SAP subsidiary established earlier this year. As a regulated payment-service provider, Tereina enables SAP to deliver services natively within finance workflows rather than relying solely on third-party providers. This helps keep payment execution, reconciliation, controls, and auditability connected to the underlying business transaction. 

 The service supports EFT, wire transfers, checks, and stablecoin-based settlement for cross-border transactions. More broadly, SAP offers customers a wide range of payment options, spanning bank API integrations, connectivity to more than 10,000 financial institutions through SWIFT, digital-currency payments, and now natively embedded payment services. 

 For finance organizations, the opportunity is not simply faster payment execution. It is reducing the effort required to connect systems, manage exceptions, and reconcile information after the fact while keeping payment processing, reconciliation, controls, and auditability within a single workflow. 

 SAP Pay is now generally available in the United States and the United Kingdom. 

 Connecting performance management across the enterprise 

 The same challenge appears across enterprise performance management. 

 Planning, consolidation, close processes, and external reporting all rely on the same financial reality. Yet they are often managed through separate tools, data models, and processes. Maintaining a consistent view of performance can become increasingly difficult as organizations grow and business conditions change. 

 At SAP Connect, we announced SAP Enterprise Financial Consolidation to help address that challenge. 

 Built on SAP Business Data Cloud , the solution brings together statutory and management consolidation with close and disclosure capabilities on a common governed data foundation. By connecting these activities more closely, finance teams can spend less time reconciling information and more time understanding performance and responding to change. 

 The solution also includes new Joule Assistants for consolidation and disclosure processes. These assistants help identify anomalies, resolve exceptions, and support disclosure preparation while maintaining auditability and human oversight. 

 For organizations operating mixed environments–some SAP, some non-SAP environments–SAP Enterprise Financial Consolidation provides flexibility by supporting data from multiple sources. It also offers a path forward for customers looking to modernize existing consolidation environments and adopt a more AI-enabled approach to performance management. 

 SAP Early Adopter Care is planned for the first quarter of 2027. 

 Expanding AI across finance and governance 

 AI’s potential in finance extends beyond answering questions or generating summaries. The larger opportunity is helping teams complete work that has traditionally required significant manual effort, specialist knowledge, and cross-functional coordination. 

 At SAP Connect, SAP expanded its portfolio of Joule Assistants to address these opportunities. 

 The new assistants support areas including accounting, revenue recognition, pricing, disclosure management, project operations, governance, and trade compliance. Embedded directly into existing workflows, they are designed to help teams complete tasks more efficiently while preserving review processes and accountability. 

 Some focus on helping finance professionals understand complex calculations and reporting requirements. Others support pricing decisions, disclosure preparation, project execution, and continuous monitoring of risks and controls. 

 Just as important is governance. 

 As organizations deploy more AI agents across business functions, they need assurance that those agents operate within the same boundaries that govern human users. New governance, security, and compliance assistants are designed to extend existing controls, access management, and monitoring capabilities to AI-driven activities, helping organizations apply consistent oversight across both human and digital actors. 

 General availability for the Governance Assistant and International Trade Assistant is planned for Q4 2026. 

 From financial insight to immediate action 

 Finance has always played a central role in helping organizations understand performance. Increasingly, it is also expected to help organizations respond in real time. 

 That makes speed, visibility, and execution just as important as reporting accuracy. 

 The innovations SAP announced at SAP Connect reflect that shift. Whether simplifying payments, connecting performance management processes, or embedding AI directly into everyday finance work, each reduces the operational distance between identifying an issue and acting on it. 

 For finance teams, the ultimate goal is not simply faster processes or faster reports. It is making better decisions with greater confidence and executing those decisions with less friction. 

 Learn more about how SAP is helping organizations modernize finance operations across ERP, planning, treasury, payments, and accounting here . 

 Lawrence Martin is general manager and chief product officer for SAP Finance & Spend. 
 David Imbert is chief marketing officer for SAP Financial Management.

title: SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 Release: Delivering the Future of Human Capital Management
author: Rebecca Carr
text:
As workforce challenges continue to outpace traditional HR processes, the organizations that lead won’t be the ones with the most AI. They’ll be the ones that understand their people, their skills, and how work really gets done—and know where AI can move them beyond incremental improvement into lasting transformation. 
 Turn HR into a strategic growth engine with AI 

 Discover Autonomous HCM 

 With the SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 release and throughout the remainder of the year, we’re taking the next step toward Autonomous HCM , bringing together agentic AI, trusted workforce data, and HR applications to help deliver the outcomes that matter most to organizations. At its core are three pillars: automate the HR function to release capacity from administrative work, redesign how tasks, workflows, roles, and teams are structured across people and AI, and reinvent how organizations recruit, develop, move, and reward their people. 

 This vision comes to life through Joule Assistants working together across SAP applications to help carry out end-to-end HR processes and help people make better decisions, faster, all within a single workspace: Joule Work . This is what it looks like when AI works across an organization’s data, applications, and processes: not more AI for the sake of AI, but AI that delivers impact you can measure. 

 Building on the SAP investments organizations have already made, the innovations we’re delivering throughout the second half of 2026 help automate, redesign, and reinvent work to realize the full promise of Autonomous HCM. 

 These innovations span the full employee lifecycle: 

 Plan & hire 

 Finding, hiring, and onboarding the right talent gets easier and faster, with every step aligned to business needs. 

 As AI drives up application volumes, recruiters risk spending more time clearing a queue than assessing if a hire works for the business. Winston Screen can address this with repeatable, configurable screening that helps narrow large applicant pools to a focused shortlist. Winston Match builds on that, with results now fully reportable in Report Builder, giving recruiters visibility into the reasoning behind AI-assisted decisions. Together, they help free up the time and attention to do what the business actually needs—apply their judgement to identify and engage the candidates most likely to succeed. 

 Shortlisting candidates with Winston Screen 

 SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors helps put agentic capability directly inside the recruiter workflow so hiring never loses momentum, with Winston Companion monitoring pipelines and booking interviews through agentic scheduling, Winston Interview delivering a conversational AI-led screening experience, and the Interview Summary Agent automatically capturing and posting a structured summary to the candidate profile. 

 Helping new hires get up to speed and start contributing faster, the Onboarding Assistant equips HR teams to deliver personalized, timely onboarding at scale, with intelligent prioritization, simplified onboarding task creation, and automated custom form conversion. 

 Manage & pay 

 These innovations help organizations work more efficiently and stay compliant while giving employees fast, seamless support to reduce the routine inquiry burden on HR teams. 

 The Payroll Assistant helps build trust in payroll so employees can have confidence in every paycheck. Administrators can quickly identify anomalies, resolve issues, and stay ahead of compliance, while employees can get direct access to clear, confident answers about their pay without raising a support ticket. 

 Payroll readiness check with the Payroll Assistant 

 The HR Operations Assistant can reduce manual effort, prevent bottlenecks, and keep HR processes moving, proactively resolving workforce and payroll data issues, automating employee and job changes, and streamlining position management. It can also detect approval bottlenecks, nudge approvers, and recommend next steps. 

 The HR System Assistant can give HR administrators a smarter way to manage day-to-day system operations—from audit readiness and compliance tracking to time and benefits configurations—reducing routine maintenance and helping HR teams drive continuous improvement and innovation. 

 Develop & grow 

 These innovations connect skill-building, learning, and career development into a more intentional experience designed for continuous growth. 

 The Learning Assistant helps move organizations to proactive workforce readiness, connecting compliance monitoring, upskilling, and development in one experience. It can guide the right learning actions at the right time for employees, managers, and admins, from flagging compliance deadlines to identifying skill gaps and recommending targeted learning. 

 People perform at their best when they know their employer is invested in their development. The Career and Talent Development Assistant helps employees close skill gaps, build personalized development plans, and set meaningful goals. For leaders, conversational talent discovery through Joule helps surface internal candidates, successors, and experts with a clear explanation of what shaped each result, helping organizations match the right talent to opportunities and grow people from within. 

 Finding internal candidates with the Career and Talent Development Assistant 

 The next step toward Autonomous HCM 

 These are not standalone capabilities. Together, they are Autonomous HCM in action: AI working with trusted data and HR processes to remove friction, surface insight, and give people the space to focus on outcomes that matter. The organizations building that way today are the ones that will lead tomorrow.
